title: Handley Page Hampden AT110
memorial_details:
The memorial is a polished steel plaque with an RAF wings badge and a Hampden outline, set into the sloping top of a rough-hewn stone block on a concrete base. It stands beside Sea Road near the junction with Longbrook, Felpham.

IWM records this as the third version of the plaque. A new plaque was made around 2019 with spelling corrected. The second sits on a wooden backboard on the wall behind. The first was wall mounted with slightly different wording and no backboard. IWM lists the condition as Good.

The plaque was first on a wall at the corner with Longbrook, which became overgrown. The local RAFA branch moved it to a low plinth close to the road. No source read gives a maker or an unveiling date for the first plaque.
inscription: New plaque: THIS PLAQUE COMMEMORATES THE LOSS OF/ THE CREW OF A HAMPDEN BOMBER OF/ 144 SQUADRON, ROYAL AIR FORCE,/ CLOSE TO THIS MEMORIAL ON 14th APRIL 1942/ THE TWIN ENGINE BOMBER (SERIAL No AT110) WAS/ EN ROUTE FROM NORTH LUFFENHAMHAM (RUTLAND)/ TO ATTACK THE PORT OF LE HAVRE IN FRANCE/ AN ENGINE FIRE WAS THE SUSPECTED CAUSE/ THE CREW WERE:/ TANGMERE MILITARY AVIATION MUSEUM/ FELPHAM PARISH COUNCIL/ SNOOKS CORNER COMMUNITY CENTRE/ ANONYMOUS DONOR/ RAF ASSOCIATION - BOGNOR REGIS BRANCH/ Old plaque: THIS PLAQUE COMMEMORATES THE SACRIFICE OF/ THE CREW OF A HAMPDEN BOMBER OF 144 SQUADRON/ WHICH CRASHED NEAR THIS SPOT ON 14th APRIL 1942/ THIS TWIN ENGINE BOMBER (Serial No. AT110)/ HAD TAKEN OFF FROM NORTH LUTHAM [sic] (RUTLAND)/ TO BOMB DORTMUND GERMANY. THE FULL REASON/ WHY IT CRASHED HERE MAY NEVER BE KNOWN./ THE CREW WERE:-/ TANGMERE MILITARY AVIATION MUSEUM/ FELPHAM PARISH COUNCIL/ SNOOKS CORNER COMMUNITY GROUP/ ANONYMOUS DONOR
narrative:
Hampden AT110 of 144 Squadron, 5 Group, took off from RAF North Luffenham on 14 April 1942 on a night operation. The IBCC Losses Database gives the target as Dortmund. The current plaque at Felpham says Le Havre, while the earlier plaque said Dortmund, so the target is not yet settled.

The aircraft crashed at 2215 at Felpham, between Bognor Regis and Middleton-on-Sea. All four crew died. The current plaque gives an engine fire as the suspected cause. The earlier plaque said the full reason may never be known.

The pilot was Sergeant Stanley Wilson Charles Culmer, aged 26, buried at West Wickham (St John the Baptist) Churchyard. Sergeant Ronald Edward George Nation, the observer, was 21 and is buried at Bristol (Canford) Cemetery. Sergeant James Aitken Hutchison, wireless operator and air gunner, was 25 and is buried at North Berwick. Sergeant Dennis Manning, air gunner, was 21 and is buried at Stoak (St Laurence) Churchyard.

community_connection:
The current plaque credits Tangmere Military Aviation Museum, Felpham Parish Council, Snooks Corner Community Centre, an anonymous donor and the RAF Association Bognor Regis Branch. The earlier plaque credited the museum, the parish council, Snooks Corner Community Group and an anonymous donor.

No custodian is confirmed. War Memorials Online lists the custodian as Information Required and IWM states no maintainer. The only body shown acting on the plaque is the local RAFA branch, which moved it.
